facts.text: I cut my head when I fell.
It's on the right side, at my temple.
I haven't had any stomach or bowel symptoms.
Three weeks ago I was in hospital with a fracture on the right side of my skull after a fall.

facts.item: knocked out in the earlier fall
facts.text: In that earlier fall I was knocked out for a short time.
I take candesartan for my blood pressure.
I take metformin for my diabetes.
I don't take any water pills.
As far as I know, I don't have kidney disease.
I live in a nursing home.

findings.name: hydration assessment
findings.result: Dry mucous membranes; reduced skin turgor.

findings.name: metabolic panel
findings.result: Sodium 118 meq/L; potassium 3.6 meq/L; creatinine 0.9 mg/dL; blood urea nitrogen 7 mg/dL; glucose 101 mg/dL.

findings.name: noncontrast CT of the head
findings.result: No acute hemorrhage or edema; new right frontal hygroma; stable posterior fossa Dandy-Walker cyst; known parietal impression fracture unchanged.

findings.name: orthostatic test
findings.result: Supine: blood pressure 123/71 mmHg, pulse 83/min. After 2 minutes standing: 75/52 mmHg, pulse 100/min; the patient became dizzy and the test was stopped. Immediately on returning supine: 115/75 mmHg, 90/min. (Serum sodium at the time 129 meq/L.)

findings.name: serum sodium at the earlier admission

aliases: cerebral salt wasting after head injury
gold.reasoning: 1. Rule out iso- or hyperosmolar hyponatremia — “measurement of serum osmolality ... shows no significant osmolar gap. These findings identify the case as a hypoosmolar hyponatremia and rule out the presence of an osmolar gap.” 2. Identify hypovolemia — “The low blood pressure, orthostatic hypotension ... decreased skin turgor, and absence of peripheral edema identify the volume status as hypovolemic.” 3. Exclude chronic renal disease — “in the absence of ... chronic renal disease ... cerebral salt wasting emerges as the most plausible cause.” 4. Exclude SIADH — “The clear establishment of the presence of hypovolemia ... leaves no doubt that his hyponatremia was not caused by SIADH.” 5. Support CSW in CNS disease — “in a patient with cerebral pathology, hypovolemia, and renal salt wasting ... cerebral salt wasting emerges as the most plausible cause of the prevailing hyponatremia.”

quotes.f010: Three weeks earlier, he had been hospitalized for a traumatic right-sided parietal skull impression fracture after a fall
quotes.f017: had no known chronic kidney disease

x018.source_text: On hospital day 6, with serum sodium at 129 meq/L, an orthostatic test showed supine blood pressure 123/71 mmHg with pulse 83/min, dropping to 75/52 mmHg with pulse 100/min after 2 minutes of standing; the patient became dizzy and the test was stopped. / Immediately on returning to supine, vitals returned to 115/75 mmHg and 90/min.

x019.source_text: hyponatremia was noted then but untreated

x018: Performed on hospital day 6, after some days of in-hospital care; the serum sodium of 129 meq/L at that time reflects the hospital course and is kept only as context of the test, not as its own sodium record.
x019: The earlier admission's hyponatremia has no value; it is a finding from before the index visit.

source_issues: s008 holds two sentences (admission laboratory studies; urine studies 10 hours later).
notes: Index visit: the emergency department visit after the fall with a head laceration (s001, s003-s010); the orthostatic test on hospital day 6 (s011-s012) is a timed finding.
The hyponatremia noted at the earlier admission (s002) is a finding with time, not a patient fact: the source does not say he was told about it.
The earlier skull fracture and its brief loss of consciousness are medical-history facts; 'dizziness without syncope' gives dizziness present and fainting absent for the current episode.
The examination of s007 is split by region: hydration signs, neck veins, legs, lungs and the unremarkable remainder.
